How to Submit Public Comment:
Members of the Public who wish to submit public comment may do so using one of the following
methods. Public comment is limited to the time allotted.

In-Person: Complete a Speaker Card, indicating the agenda item number and submit it to the City
Clerk prior to the meeting. Speakers shall be limited to three (3) minutes per person per item. At the
Mayor’ s discretion, the time limit may be shortened to allow all speakers to address the City Council.

Electronic submission of Public Comment is also available via the City’s website as noted below.
Public Comment submitted electronically will be read into the record. Words that would disrupt the
meeting, including profanity, obscenity, and discriminatory language, will not be read. Your
comments must be received by 5:00 P.M. on meeting day.

Website: Please submit your comments using the online public comment form at Public Comment.

Watch the Meeting Online

   MINUTES OF APRIL 3, 2023
 REGULAR MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL COMMUNITY SERVICES COMMISSION

CALL TO ORDER

Chair Huerta called the special meeting of the Community Services Commission to order at 6:32
P.M. on Monday, April 3, 2023, with Commissioners and staff in the Council Chamber at City
Hall, 425 South Mission Drive, San Gabriel, California, 91776.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Commissioner Cordero.

ROLL CALL

Commissioners Present:  Cheryl Anne Cabot, Catherine Cordero, Theresa Huerta,
  and Ting Xie

Commissioners Absent:  None

ANNOUNCEMENTS
Manager Morales-Stevens provided information for the public on how to submit comments, and
how to request meeting agendas. If you wish to address the Community Services Commission,
email all public comments to CSCommission@sgch.org.

1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  The Agenda Order was approved by the Commission.

2. PUBLIC COMMENT

  Public Comment: None

3. ACTION ITEMS

COMMUNITY SERVICES COMMISSION REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  APRIL 3, 2023
   A. APPROVAL MINUTES

  A motion was made by Commissioner Cabot, seconded by Commissioner
  Cordero to approve the minutes of the Community Services Commission
  Meeting for March 6, 2023.

  Motion approved as presented by a vote of 4-0-0 as follows:

  AYES:  CABOT, CORDERO, HUERTA, XIE
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE

4. DISCUSSION ITEMS

  A. DISCUSSION OF 2023 ANNUAL WORKPLAN
  Manager Morales-Stevens presented the item.

  The commission reviewed and discussed the results from the HEAR Commission
  Engagement Survey. They would like to conduct a survey during Spring
  Celebration on April 8.

  The Commission discussed ways to get more participation in community
  events. Vice Chair Xie shared that she has a contact with a counselor from
  Gabrielino High School that can potentially utilize students’ help with
  translation for public meeting agendas and event flyers.

  The commissioners provided an update regarding discretionary funding for
  Smith Park Pool. They suggested the funding request umbrella be expanded.

  Public Comment: None

  B. MONTLY DEPARTMENT REPORT
  Manager Morales-Stevens provided the report.

  Public Comment: None

5. COMMISSIONER REPORTS

  Commissioner Cabot visited a pop-up bookstore event at the Blossom Market
  Hall, and she was interested in a bookstore in El Monte which had a nice display
  and representation.

COMMUNITY SERVICES COMMISSION REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  APRIL 3, 2023
   Commissioner Cordero plans to attend the Spring Celebration and will be
  attending the Pentathlon event next year.

  Vice Chair Xie attended the Pentathlon at Jefferson Middle School. She thanked
  Supervisor Cortez and the team for the lively event. On the same day, she also
  attended the 13th Annual Native Voices Short Play Festival at the Autry Museum
  of the American West.

  Chair Huerta expressed appreciation to Community Services staff for creating a
  lot of incredible programs. She commended Recreational Leaders for helping
  the kids with confidence building through sportsmanship.

6. STAFF COMMENTS

  A. DATES TO REMEMBER
  Manager Morales-Stevens presented the item.

  Public Comment: None

COMMUNITY SERVICES COMMISSION REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  AUGUST 7, 2023
 3. ACTION ITEMS

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A motion was made by Vice Chair Xie, seconded by Commissioner Cabot to
  approve the minutes of the Community Services Commission Meeting for June
  5, 2022.

  Motion approved as presented by a vote of 5-0-0 as follows:

  AYES:  BARRANTES, CABOT, DUONG, HUERTA, XIE
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE

4. DISCUSSION ITEMS
  A. COMMISSION REORGANIZATION
  Manager Morales-Stevens presented the process of Chair and Vice Chair
  selection.

  Chair Huerta nominated Ting Xie for Chair, and the nomination was accepted.

  Ting Xie was appointed as Chair by acclamation.

  Commissioner Huerta nominated Nancy Duong for Vice Chair, and the
  nomination was accepted.

  Nancy Duong was appointed as Vice Chair by acclamation.

  B. DISCUSSION OF 2023 ANNUAL WORKPLAN

  The Commission continued working on getting funds for the pool and believed
  that more effort should be made to get more funds for the pool. The
  Commission reviewed funding reports from other cities, and they seem to have
  received more funds since they requested funding from different sources. The
  Commission suggested the City do the same for successful funding.

  The Commission inquired about the status of the Translation Volunteer
  Program, and Manager Morales-Stevens presented the requirements and
  benefits of being a volunteer for this program and the onboarding orientation
  process. The commission believed that this would be a great assistance in event
  flyer translations. Vice Chair Duong suggested to have Vietnamese translation

COMMUNITY SERVICES COMMISSION REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  AUGUST 7, 2023
   if possible, and Commissioner Huerta mentioned she had a contact that might
  be able to help with Vietnamese translation.

  The Commission discussed how they would like to get more involved in public
  and City events by having a Community Services booth. They suggested having
  a banner for the booth to attract more attendance. The Commission also
  discussed ways to find out what the social needs are for the senior community,
  so they would like to conduct surveys at different programs and events hosted
  by the City. The Commission also suggested conducting surveys to RideSG
  users and have the surveys on Grapevine Press which can be passed out to
  areas with higher senior population such as adult daycares or Hawaii
  supermarket and can be dropped off at the Community Services office after.

  The Commission was able to conduct the surveys and get a good turnaround
  at the National Night Out on August 1, 2023, and was excited for the results to
  come out. The Commission suggested conducting another survey at the Mental
  Wellness Expo on October 1, 2023.

  Public Comment: None

  C. SUMMER PROGRAM UPDATE

  Manager Morales-Stevens presented the item.

  The Commission discussed ways to improve the Summer Camp by potentially
  raising fees to provide more staff and improve efficiencies and having a scaling
  fee for low-income families. The commission was also hoping to have more
  recreation swim hours available and possibly more affordable swimming passes
  for purchase.

  The Commission commended staff for their great work to make the programs
  and events run smoothly. They suggested bringing more local businesses to
  City events and having events fliers available early, so more people are
  informed.

  D. MONTLY DEPARTMENT REPORT
  Manager Morales-Stevens provided the report.

  Public Comment: None

COMMUNITY SERVICES COMMISSION REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  AUGUST 7, 2023
 5. COMMISSIONER REPORTS

  Commissioner Cabot expressed appreciation for Commissioner Huerta for
  serving as Commission Chair for the last term. She also commended Community
  Services Staff for their hard work, and she would be helping at the Backpack
  giveaway. She will also continue to work on funding for the pool.

  Commissioner Huerta worked with San Gabriel Mission church to partner with
  a small group of private Mental Health providers to host the Team Depression
  Symposium Routines on July 22, 2023. There were about 36 people in
  attendance. She thought that was a great event, and the team was committed
  to work harder with the expectation to provide the support to the residents of
  San Gabriel.

  Commissioner Huerta reported that the Walk to LA event would not be hosted
  this year. She provided an update that San Gabriel Mission Church opened on
  July 1, 2023, and self-guided tours and new exhibits are now available. She
  recommended checking out the exhibit as it is short but full of information.

  Chair Xie attended the Kids’ Day and 4th of July event hosted by the City. She
  also attended July Membership Meeting of Women Political Caucus SGB with
  Special Speaker Garcia Noma with the goal of raising awareness of reducing
  water usage.

  On July 29, 2023, Chair Xie attended the 6th US Legacy Art Festival Opening
  Ceremony in San Gabriel focusing on cultural exchange promotion of local
  citizens and international visitors.

  On July 30, 2023, Chair Xie and her husband organized an event called San
  Gabriel for Change to perform community cleanup at Vincent Lugo Park with 30
  other participants from Gabrielino High School and San Gabriel High School.
  She reported that homelessness was still an issue close to Vincent Lugo Park,
  and there were also some pothole and low fencing issues that she was hoping
  should be fixed by the private agency who owns the property.

6. STAFF COMMENTS

  Manger Morales-Stevens commended all Community Services staff for their
  hard work to make sure all programs in the summer went smoothly, and he was
  hoping with the two new supervisors soon to be onboarded, the department
  will be fully staffed, and there will be positive changes, and the department will
  be able to offer new or better programs to the community.

COMMUNITY SERVICES COMMISSION REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  AUGUST 7, 2023
 7. ADJOURNMENT

  Chair Xie adjourned the meeting at 9:05 p.m.

  Next regular meeting held on Monday, October 2, 2023, in the Council Chamber
  at City Hall, 425 South Mission Drive, San Gabriel, California, 91776, at 6:30 pm.

_____________________________________
Meyling Suy, Commission Clerk

Approved this 2nd day of October 2023:

_____________________________________
Ting Xie, Commission Chair

  MEMORANDUM
DATE:  March 6, 2023

TO:  Community Services Commission

FROM:  Rebecca Perez, Community Services Director

BY:  Christina Alatorre, Recreation Supervisor

SUBJECT:  Discussion of the 2023 Annual Workplan

SUMMARY
This is the Annual Workplan developed by the Community Services Commission and is
intended for the 2023 calendar year. The Community Services Commission approved the
2023 Workplan on December 5, 2022, which was originally carried over from the 2022
Annual Workplan. The 2022 Annual Workplan was approved by the City Council during
the September 6, 2022 City Council meeting.

PURPOSE OF THE COMMISSION
The purpose of the Community Services Commission is to creatively and inclusively
explore ways in which the Community Services Department can enrich quality of life for
residents of the City of San Gabriel by providing equitable access to dynamic programs,
services and spaces that strengthen community connection and engagement.

SCOPE OF THE COMMISSION
The Community Services Commission serves as an advisory body to the Community
Services Department and City Council, and functions as a liaison between residents and
city government. It is the responsibility of the Community Services Commission to
advocate on behalf of the San Gabriel community and to ensure that the Community
Services Department’s programs, services, spaces and events advance the Commission’s
purpose.

Purpose of the Annual Workplan
The Annual Workplan is intended to guide the work of the Community Services
Commission and outline the areas of focus for 2023. It includes proposed programs and
projects that will be implemented and completed throughout the year.

  4-B
 APPROVED ANNUAL WORKPLAN 2023
The 2023 Workplan sets forth five priority areas as identified in the Community Services
Strategic Plan for the Community Services Department. The following list of ideas,
programs and activities are not intended to be exhaustive or to limit the action items the
Commission can explore.

1. Create New Innovative Programs and Services to Engage the Entire Community
  a. Develop and implement pop-up events or host an information booth at
  events publicizing all transportation services offered in the City
  b. Collaborate with businesses/organizations in order to offer additional social
  services to older adults
  i. For example: Collaborating with businesses offering tracking
  devices/systems for older adults with memory related health issues
  c. Develop an internship program for youth to assist with translation services

2. Connect the Entire Community to Enhance Quality of Life
  a. Continue to support health services by partnering with health service
  providers
  i. Examples include: Herald Christian and USC School of Pharmacy
  b. Develop and implement a Community Services Department Day advertising
  all programs, events and services offered by the Community Services Department
  c. Connect all geographic areas of the City
  i. Examples include: Hosting events and programs in the South San Gabriel
  area and various other neighborhoods

3. Embrace and Celebrate Community Diversity
  a. Propose a Moon Festival to be held in the Mission District; due to the potential
  budget impact of this event, the proposal would need to be brought forward to
  the City Council for implementation
  b. Partner and collaborate with various cultural and interfaith organizations to
  assist in the development and implementation of events and services
  i. Examples include: Partnering with the HEAR Commission, Native American
  Community and interfaith groups

4. Plan and Create New and Enhanced Open Spaces, Parks and Community Facilities
  a. Enhance current park spaces

  4-B
   i. Examples include: Enhancement of Smith Park and updating Community
  Services facilities
  b. Seek additional park spaces and amenities
  i. Examples include: Dog area and rubberized running trail

5. Develop Innovative Resources and Tools to Achieve our Mission
  a. Collect survey data with targeted questions to improve, enhance and seek
  additional services as needed
  b. Identify community leaders and organizations to offer additional resources
  c. Utilize social platforms to reach various audiences
  i. For example: Utilizing WeChat social media
  d. Cross promote programs through various City Departments
  i. For example: utilize Police Department’s Neighborhood Watch to
  disseminate information

FISCAL IMPACT
Should the following items be included in the Annual Workplan, staff and the Commission
recognize that there may be fiscal impacts:
• Develop and implement a Community Services Department Day advertising all
programs, events and services offered by the Community Services Department
• Propose a Moon Festival to be held in the Mission District
• Enhance current park spaces
• Seek additional park spaces and amenities

Once staff and the Commission determine the associated cost for these items, should they
not fall within the existing department budget, staff will present the items to the City
Council at a later date for possible budgetary allocation, review and approval.

  MEMORANDUM
DATE:  October 2, 2023

TO:  Community Services Commission

FROM:  Matthew Morales-Stevens, Community Services Manager

SUBJECT:  Monthly Department Report- October 2023

Older Adults
The City of San Gabriel in partnership with the YWCA of San Gabriel Valley hosted the
Moon Festival special luncheon with 85 seniors in attendance. Moon cakes and fruit were
provided by the US Chinese Women’s Organization. The next special luncheon will be the
“Spooky Luncheon” on October 16.

Discover San Gabriel
The new publication Discover San Gabriel (Discover SG) replaces the Grapevine Guide and
Grapevine Newsletter. The first edition, Fall 2023, was released digitally on the City website
September 15 and hard copies reached the Community Services office and the post office
for delivery to all San Gabriel homes September 29. Discover SG includes City News
translated in Spanish and Chinese, classes, event information and community resources.

Special Events
Upcoming events include the Dia de Los Muertos Celebration on November 2 from 6pm-
8:30pm in the Mission Playhouse. The event will feature live performances by Ballet
Folklorico and Los Colibri. Community members are encouraged to submit a photo of
their loved one for display on the community altar. New to the event this year- El Pavo
Bakery will have food available for purchase including tamales, café de olla, hot chocolate
and much more.

Fall Fun Festival will take place on October 27 from 5pm-9pm and will include a costume
contest, haunted zone, food trucks, trunk or treat and carnival games. A haunted tour of
the Mission Playhouse will also be offered. Community members interested in
participating in the costume contest or haunted zone are encouraged to pre-register.
Limited space will be available on the day of the event.

Turkey Trot is scheduled for November 18 with runs starting at 7am. The event includes a
Kids 1k, 5k walk/run and 10k run. Registration includes a commemorative event t-shirt,
 finisher medal, raffle prize entry and light refreshments. Pre-registration ends October 20
and is the last day a shirt and medal is guaranteed to be received on the day of the event.
